questions.stem: According to the passage, why did the Wright brothers choose Kitty Hawk, North Carolina to test their flying machine?
options: It had the best wind conditions for testing flight
It was close to their home in Dayton, Ohio
It already had a museum for airplanes
The French government suggested the location
questions.evidence: The best place with the best wind conditions seemed to be a piece of sandy land in North Carolina along the coast of the Atlantic Ocean.
questions.explanation_ko: 본문에서 Kitty Hawk 근처의 모래땅이 바람 조건이 가장 좋았다고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT true about the events of December 17th, 1903?
options: Orville flew the plane for about 12 seconds
The brothers made a total of four flights that day
Wilbur personally took photographs of the flight
Four other men watched the flights
questions.evidence: One of the men took pictures.
questions.explanation_ko: 사진을 찍은 사람은 지켜보던 다른 네 사람 중 한 명이지 윌버가 아니었습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the fact that few newspapers noted the first flight and it took almost five years for the brothers to become famous?
options: The public and press did not immediately understand the importance of the achievement
The Wright brothers deliberately hid their invention from the press
The first flight was considered a failure by observers
Newspapers were banned from covering aviation news
questions.evidence: It was almost five years before the Wright brothers became famous.
questions.explanation_ko: 몇 안 되는 신문만이 보도했고 유명해지기까지 5년이 걸렸다는 점에서, 당시 사람들이 그 업적의 중요성을 즉시 알아채지 못했음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that visitors to the museum can also see space vehicles and a rock collected from the moon?
options: To show how much aviation and space technology have advanced since the Wright brothers' first flight
To explain how the Wright brothers helped design space vehicles
To compare the weight of the moon rock to the Wright brothers' airplane
To argue that the museum should focus more on space exploration
questions.evidence: The world has changed a lot since Wilbur and Orville Wright began the modern age of flight over one hundred years ago.
questions.explanation_ko: 우주선과 달의 돌을 언급함으로써 라이트 형제의 첫 비행 이후 항공우주 기술이 얼마나 발전했는지를 보여주려는 의도입니다.

questions.stem: In the sentence "Few newspapers, however, noted the event," the word "noted" is closest in meaning to which of the following?
options: reported on
criticized
misunderstood
celebrated
questions.evidence: Few newspapers, however, noted the event.

blanks.meaning: 공기보다 무거운 (기구가 아닌 기계식 비행기를 뜻함)
blanks.sentence_ko: 1903년 12월 17일, 그들은 공기보다 무겁고 엔진으로 동력을 얻는 기계로 세계 최초의 비행을 했다.
윌버와 오빌 라이트는 작은 엔진 동력 비행 기계를 만든 미국의 발명가들이다.

key_points: The Wright brothers built and flew the first engine-powered, heavier-than-air airplane on December 17, 1903, at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.
They developed their ideas through earlier experiments with kites, a toy helicopter, and gliders.
Their first flight lasted only 12 seconds and covered 36 meters, and they made three more flights that day.
The achievement went largely unnoticed by the press, and it took nearly five years for the brothers to become famous.
Wilbur's 1908 demonstration flights in France and Orville's flights in the U.S. brought them worldwide fame.
Their original airplane is now displayed in the Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C., alongside modern space vehicles.
main_idea: Wilbur and Orville Wright invented and flew the first successful engine-powered airplane, achieving a breakthrough that eventually made them world-famous and began the modern age of flight.
restate_sentence: On December 17th, 1903, they made the world's first flight in a machine that was heavier than air and powered by an engine.
